Design an implementation plan (read-only: do not edit files) for the FRONTEND of a hackathon product. Deadline: ~10 hours from now. Repo: /Users/akshatkhair/Documents/Projects/temporal_ai_error404.ai

## Product
error404.ai: Deutsche Bahn journey-reliability predictor. Traveller shares a multi-leg DB connection text from the DB app into our PWA; app parses it into per-leg cards; backend predicts each train's delay, chains them into "Probability your plan fails: NN%", and gives plain-language advice. The team will ALSO present the pitch directly from this app on a projector, so it needs a presenter mode.

## User's brief (verbatim intent)
"minimalistic and super interactive with real view of map and zooming in into earth for the route; we will use this platform for presenting directly as well". Web + installable PWA (no native apps).

## Demo shot list (team-setup/state/02-demo-script/demo-script.md)
0:00 pain (photo of real DB journey) → 0:10 share from DB app into our PWA (web share target) → 0:20 parsed journey as per-leg cards (train, from→to, planned times, transfer) → 0:30 per-train predicted delay with the chain visualised (train 1 late → transfer shrinks → train 3 missed), headline "Probability your plan fails: NN%" → 0:45 recommendation ("take the earlier IC, 25 min more buffer") with tap → alternative connection → 0:60 proof: our model vs GPT/Claude baseline, one chart one number → 0:75 close: "not 'it will rain' — 'take an umbrella'", installed PWA icon.

## Contract (DRAFT, code against it; team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md)
```ts
type Station = { evaNumber: string; name: string };
type Leg = { trainId: string; from: Station; to: Station; plannedDeparture: string; plannedArrival: string; transferMinutes?: number };
type Journey = { id: string; legs: Leg[]; source: "db-share" | "manual" | "seed" };
type Explained<T> = { value: T; reasoning: string; sources: string[]; confidence: "low"|"medium"|"high" };
type LegDelay = { trainId: string; expectedDelayMinutes: Explained<number>; missProbability: Explained<number> };
type Prediction = { journeyId: string; legs: LegDelay[]; planFailProbability: Explained<number>; modelId: string };
type Recommendation = { verdict: "good"|"add-buffer"|"take-alternative"; advice: Explained<string>; bufferMinutes?: number; alternative?: Journey };
```
Endpoints on the Node backend (port 8000): GET /api/health, POST /api/journeys/parse {text}→Journey, POST /api/predict Journey→Prediction, POST /api/recommend {journey,prediction}→Recommendation, GET /api/seed/demo→Journey. The backend is being built in parallel with mocks; assume it exists. We plan to add `lat`/`lon` (optional) to Station in the backend responses so the frontend can draw the route; frontend should also have its own station-coordinates fallback table.

## Constraints / facts discovered
- `app/frontend/` is a placeholder: package.json with `_hackos_placeholder: true`, `src/features/_TEMPLATE/{components,hooks}`. Convention (app/frontend/README.md): one folder per feature under `src/features/<name>/`, names matching backend feature names: `pwa-shell`, `share-parser`, `delay-prediction`, `recommendation`. Owners file is blank; we will claim frontend.
- A working React 19 + Vite 8 + Tailwind 4 + shadcn (new-york, neutral) + TypeScript 7 setup exists at `team-setup/board/web/` (package.json, vite.config.ts with `@` alias, strictPort 5173, `/api` proxy, components.json, src/index.css with Tailwind v4 @theme). Mirror it; do NOT modify it. Read those files to copy exact config.
- Backend has NO CORS and NO static serving. Dev: Vite proxy `/api` → http://127.0.0.1:8000. Demo: backend will serve `app/frontend/dist` statically (same origin needed for service worker + share target). Phone share-target needs HTTPS: plan for `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8000` quick tunnel.
- No geo data in repo. Storyline route not picked yet; likely a German city → Zürich HB (event is in Zurich; hook "too frustrated to come to Zurich"). Candidate seed: Berlin Hbf → Frankfurt(Main) Hbf (ICE) → Basel SBB (ICE) → Zürich HB (IC). Plan a hand-authored `stations.json` with ~40 major DE/CH/AT hubs (name, evaNumber if known, lat, lon) and name normalisation (umlauts, "Hbf", "(Main)").
- Higgsfield credits: only 110; image generations cost 1–2 credits; video ~100. Use only for app icon / maskable icon / one hero or closing backdrop (≤ ~15 credits). Do not plan generated video.
- Rule: no speculative abstractions; smoke test the happy path only. Never commit unless asked.

## Design decisions to make and justify (pick one, recommend)
1. Globe/map tech for "real map, zoom into earth to the route": options MapLibre GL JS with `projection: 'globe'` (real vector tiles, free tile source such as OpenFreeMap styles, flyTo from globe to route, GeoJSON line layers, no key), vs `cobe` (stylised dot globe, no map detail), vs react-globe.gl/three (textured sphere, no street-level), vs Cesium (heavy, key). Consider offline risk at the venue: recommend a fallback (e.g. cache tiles via service worker, or a stylised fallback) and note bundle size.
2. Visual design: dark, minimal, full-bleed globe with an overlay panel (bottom sheet on phone, right rail on desktop), large type for projector. Colour system: risk colour scale for legs (green→amber→red), DB-inspired red accent optional. Reduced-motion support.
3. Presenter mode: `?present=1` or keyboard `P`; ArrowRight/Left step through the shots above as app states with animations (globe idle → share received → legs parsed and route drawn leg by leg with flyTo → per-leg delays + chain + headline count-up → recommendation with alternative route drawn → proof chart → close slide). Must work offline from the seed journey. Also a normal user flow (share target/paste → results).
4. PWA: `manifest.webmanifest` with `share_target` (GET with `text`/`title`/`url` params, or POST multipart — pick and justify; note GET share_target is simplest for text), icons, `display: standalone`, theme colour; service worker (vite-plugin-pwa vs hand-written — pick) precaching app shell + runtime cache for tiles. Route `/share` reads the shared text and calls /api/journeys/parse.
5. Proof chart: small inline chart from a static `public/proof.json` {model, baseline, metric} rendered with plain SVG (no chart lib) — or a static PNG the ML teammate supplies. Plan both: JSON if present, else image.

## Deliverable
A step-by-step plan with: exact files to create under app/frontend (paths), the package.json dependency list with versions where known, the vite config, the component tree per feature folder, state model (a small store or React context; no Redux), the presenter state machine, the API client module, the stations table approach, the route line drawing approach (great-circle or straight segments between consecutive stations; leg colouring; animated draw), manifest + SW details, the responsive/projector layout, a time-boxed order of work (hours 1–10) with what to cut first if behind, and a verification section (npm run build, vite dev + backend, Chrome DevTools Application tab for manifest/SW, a share-target test on Android via the tunnel, keyboard walk-through of presenter mode). Be concrete; cite existing repo files to copy from.

# AGENTS.md — hack-os shared agent instructions

Single source of truth for every coding harness. `CLAUDE.md` points here.
Read this whole file once per session. These rules govern product work;
explicitly requested maintenance of hack-os itself is not constrained by
an example product's demo script or contract.

## 1. Boot sequence and freshness

local-only: no downloads, product dependency installs, git config changes,

requirements. Never silently initialize or reset an event.

Keep the reusable roster in `team.json`; assign product roles fresh per event.

For an active event, read in order:
1. `team-setup/state/pipeline.json`
2. `team-setup/state/decisions.md` — identify current, non-superseded decisions.
3. `team-setup/state/owners.md`

and whether the real contract is frozen. Missing information is unknown,
not permission to invent assignments or implement fictional requirements.

relevant task and contract. After a teammate reports a change, refresh even
in a running session. A dashboard refresh does not refresh an agent's mind.

Git is explicit synchronization, not live collaboration. `event.json`
names the coordination branch and maintainer. The maintainer integrates
accepted state changes there; teammates fetch and safely integrate before
new work and at checkpoints. Never auto-pull into a dirty worktree, discard
changes, auto-stash, or resolve another person's conflicts. Show local HEAD,
uncommitted coordination edits, and remote freshness as unknown until checked.
Offline work uses a local snapshot, never a claimed live team state.

## 2. Hackathon mode

- Write smoke tests for the demo happy path and coordination data safety.

  dependencies are separate from whichever product stack the team chooses.

  defaults. A skill does not authorize unrequested installs, data uploads,
  extra agents, destructive commands, or changes to system security controls.

Before editing, check `team-setup/state/owners.md` and the owning task in
`team-setup/board/tasks.json`. Do not edit another person's assigned files.
A sub-owner helps within an explicitly delegated boundary; they do not
redirect scope. Name owners for shared wiring, manifests and lockfiles too.
Ownership is per event, not inferred from background. Use one branch/worktree
per independent writer; worktrees alone do not sync different machines.
Reassignments and delegation must be explicit and synced before work starts.
Avoid direct file editing while a dashboard write touches the same records.

## 4. Contract rule

The real `team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md` freezes when that
gate completes. Code against it and mock missing dependencies. A required
contract change needs explicit human approval and a recorded decision.
`app/shared/` is generated from the agreed contract, never independently
patched. No sample schema, endpoint, or product stack is a requirement.

## 5. Scope rule

Product work must support the real demo script, including required setup,
seed data, deployment, accessibility and failure recovery. Ask before adding
features absent from it. Maintain `not-building.md`. Keep the deck current;
protect polish and submission time. Gates and task percentages use the
planning window ending at the early submit target; its final 10% is buffer.

## 6. Idea rule

A thought is not a decision. Record it in `team-setup/state/ideas.md` as
raised, then exploring, adopted or discarded. Only status changes in place;

answers; do not portray model confidence as a calibrated probability.

save succeeded. Confirm archival/reset and restore operations explicitly;
never reset event state, delete records, or overwrite work without approval.

`for f in bootstrap.sh team-setup/hooks/* team-setup/scripts/*.sh; do bash -n "$f" || exit 1; done` for shell syntax, and `node --check team-setup/board/app.js` when Node is available.

(typecheck + Vite build). `npm --prefix team-setup/board/web run dev` starts
both the local API and UI. Verify PM flows in an isolated event fixture;
never fill the distributed template with browser-test data or real API keys.
Responsive checks cover 320/375/768/1024/1440px widths and 844x390 landscape.
Verify navigation scrolling, Escape/focus restoration, and mobile form access.
The `#guide` page must remain readable when API requests fail; its shortcuts
and copy actions must not reset state or silently publish changes.
Product checks use `team-setup/scripts/smoke.sh`; unconfigured is not a pass.
A clean snapshot plus passing smoke is required before calling a demo ready.

# Demo script — DRAFT, freezes when the storyline route is picked

**Status:** draft. Shots are settled; the route, station names and numbers
are placeholders until the "pick the storyline route" task is done. After
that this file is frozen (AGENTS.md rule 5).

**Format:** live pitch. **Storyline route:** `<ROUTE — our biggest trouble with DB>`.

| Time | Shot | On screen |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:10 | The pain | Presenter: "I was too frustrated to come to Zurich." Photo/screenshot of the real DB journey on `<ROUTE>` with its connections. Half an hour of buffer was not enough. |
| 0:10–0:20 | Share from DB | Phone (mirrored): open the DB app, press **Share** on the connection, pick our PWA from the share sheet. |
| 0:20–0:30 | Journey extracted | Our app shows the parsed journey: each train as a card (train, from → to, planned times, transfer time). No typing. |
| 0:30–0:45 | Per-train delay | Each card gets a predicted delay from the fine-tuned model, with the chain shown: train 1 late → transfer shrinks → train 3 missed. Headline: **"Probability your plan fails: NN%"**. |
| 0:45–0:60 | Recommendation | Below the number, plain-language advice: "take the earlier IC, 25 min more buffer, you arrive relaxed" or "this connection is good". Tap → alternative connection with comfortable transfer. |
| 0:60–0:75 | Proof | Side by side: our model vs the given baseline (raw data into GPT / Claude Opus) on the Oct→Aug held-out data for `<ROUTE>`. One chart, one number. |
| 0:75–0:90 | Close | Weather-forecast line: "not 'it will rain' — 'take an umbrella'." Installed-PWA icon on the home screen. What's next: causes (level 3). |

## Minimum build list (derived from the shots)

- Shot 0:10 — PWA registered as a share target (web share target manifest); installable.
- Shot 0:20 — share-text parser: DB share text → structured journey (handles more than one connection in the text).
- Shot 0:30 — backend inference endpoint: journey → per-train delay estimate → chained failure probability; fine-tuned 0.5B / 3B model trained on `<ROUTE>` Oct→Aug data.
- Shot 0:45 — recommendation algorithm on top of the delay output; alternative-connection lookup via the timetable API.
- Shot 0:60 — evaluation script: our model vs the raw-data-into-GPT/Opus baseline, one chart.
- All shots — seed journey for `<ROUTE>` that works offline if the API is down (failure recovery).
=== not-building ===
<!-- Explicit out-of-scope list, derived from demo-script.md. -->

# Not building (for this demo)

- Native Android / iOS apps — PWA only.
- One delay for the whole journey — always per train, chained.
- On-device / in-browser inference — backend only.
- Our own journey planner or ticket exchange — we build on top of the DB app's share flow.
- (3D) map view with from → to search — idea for later, not in the demo.
- Previous/next-train delay as model input (series of delays) — imagined for later, add only if the core is done.
- Level 3 causes / disaster probability — scientific evaluation after the demo scope, not a shipped feature.
- Push notifications — only if the PWA check says they work for free; not a demo shot.
- Full network coverage — the model is trained on the one storyline route.
- Training data before October 2025 — old format, excluded.
- Anything not on the shot list in demo-script.md.

# Not building

DRAFT. No active event is configured and `demo-script.md` is still empty, so
nothing here is frozen scope. This is the cut list for the candidate
Deutsche Bahn direction logged in `../ideas.md`. Rewrite it against the real
demo script once a challenge is picked.

| Cut | Why |
|---|---|
| DB live Timetables API (DBOpenData) | Needs a developer-portal key; registration lag does not fit the build window. Static monthly parquet instead. |
| Weather, traffic or event-calendar joins | Extra sourcing and alignment work that no rubric line rewards. |
| Network graph effects (delay propagation between stations) | Interesting and large; a separate project, not a 24-hour deliverable. |
| Per-train-run sequences across stops | Too few, too irregular to need a temporal model; a text baseline would match it. |
| Any fourth question type | Three cover numeric, binary and multi-class scoring already. |
| Pretraining a time-series encoder from scratch | Only the connector projection is trained; the base model stays frozen. |
| Raw hourly partition (`raw_data/`, the bulk of the 67.6 GB) | The processed monthly files carry every column the slice needs. |
| Serving, auth, persistence, multi-user state in the demo | Single-operator demo run from one machine. |

=== parallel-work-rules ===
# Parallel Work Rules

- Use one branch/worktree per independent writer. Across machines, Git
  commits must still be pushed, integrated and pulled; worktrees are not sync.
- `event.json` names the authoritative coordination branch and maintainer.
  Everyone proposes updates; the maintainer integrates accepted records.
- Before a new task or checkpoint, inspect dirty files, fetch the agreed
  remote, safely integrate the coordination branch, then tell the running
  agent to reread decisions, owners, task and contract. Do not auto-stash,
  discard changes or resolve another person's conflicts.
- Local dashboards show local snapshots. Cached upstream counts and last-fetch
  metadata do not establish current remote freshness, especially offline.
- Ownership covers feature folders AND shared wiring, manifests and lockfiles.
  Check directory and task owners. Helpers need an explicit delegated boundary;
  they do not redirect the owner's scope. Background is not an assignment.
- Mock missing dependencies against the agreed real contract. Sample contracts
  and sample ownership are inactive, never product requirements.
- Integrate at agreed checkpoints, not only at the final integration gate.
  A complete task board is not proof that the demo works end to end.
- Record approved contract changes and supersessions explicitly. Reread them
  before the next substantial edit, even within an existing agent session.
- Dashboard stale-write checks protect local edits; Git handles cross-machine
  conflicts. Do not directly edit a file while the dashboard is writing it.
- Agent teams are off by default and optional. If enabled deliberately, split
  only within your own ownership; one human remains accountable. Check usage
  in the provider's actual usage tools, not the smoke/snapshot panel.
- No shared prompt log is required. Recent committed activity is evidence of
  recorded changes, not a claim about what a teammate is currently doing.
=== pitch-and-demo ===
# Pitch and Demo

Protect presentation time and prepare a reliable demo for each event.

## Who presents

Choose a presenter for the current event and record that assignment under
`polish-and-pitch` in `state/owners.md`. No presenter or product role is
preassigned by this template.

Keep the presenter informed throughout the event so they can explain what
was built and why. The rest of the team supports Q&A using
`08-pitch-sync.md`'s cheat sheet, built from current, non-superseded decisions.

## The deck is built in parallel from hour zero, never after

Six fixed slide slots exist from the start (`08-pitch-sync.md`), filled
continuously as the pipeline advances. There is no "build the deck at the
end" step in this system — if that's happening, something upstream didn't
run.

## Demo failure insurance list

Run through this before the `polish-and-pitch` gate ends, via
`07-demo-doctor.md`:

- **Seed script for deterministic data** — the demo never depends on live,
  unpredictable state.
- **Offline fallback path** — assume venue wifi will fail during the
  pitch. Have a path that works without it.
- **Backup video recorded** before the polish gate ends. Not "we'll record
  it if there's time" — this is a checked item, not a nice-to-have.
  Manual screen capture and voiceover are sufficient. For an optional
  automated video-production workflow, the team can evaluate
  [OpenMontage](https://github.com/calesthio/OpenMontage) separately.
  It is not vendored or installed by bootstrap; review its dependencies,
  generation-provider costs and data handling before use. It is never
  required by the demo-doctor checklist.

"""Score every model on exactly the same examples and write one comparison report."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

import metrics

COLUMNS = ["example_id", "split", "target_minutes", "cancelled", "lead_minutes", "cls", "pre_departure"]


def load_predictions(path: str) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Arrays saved by the baselines or the training script."""
    with np.load(path) as data:
        return {key: data[key] for key in data.files if key != "probs"}


def main() -> None:
    """Intersect example ids across models, score them, write JSON and Markdown."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--examples", default="data/trip/examples.parquet")
    parser.add_argument("--split", default="test")
    parser.add_argument("--model", action="append", required=True, help="name=path/to/predictions.npz")
    parser.add_argument("--out", default="out/trip/report")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    frame = pd.read_parquet(args.examples, columns=COLUMNS)
    frame = frame[frame["split"] == args.split].set_index("example_id")
    predictions = {}
    for spec in args.model:
        name, path = spec.split("=", 1)
        if Path(path).exists():
            predictions[name] = load_predictions(path)
        else:
            print(f"skipping {name}: {path} does not exist")
    common = sorted(set.intersection(*[set(p["example_id"].tolist()) for p in predictions.values()]))
    ids = np.array(common)
    subset = frame.loc[ids].reset_index()
    print(f"scoring {len(predictions)} models on {len(ids)} shared {args.split} examples")

    results = {}
    for name, pred in predictions.items():
        order = pd.Series(np.arange(len(pred["example_id"])), index=pred["example_id"]).loc[ids].to_numpy()
        p_late = pred["p_late"][order]
        results[name] = metrics.evaluate(subset, pred["quantiles"][order], pred["p_cancel"][order],
                                         None if np.isnan(p_late).all() else p_late)

    out_dir = Path(args.out)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (out_dir / f"{args.split}_metrics.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
    groups = list(next(iter(results.values())).keys())
    sections = [f"# Trip delay: {args.split} split, {len(ids)} shared examples\n",
                "Lower is better except coverage, which should be close to 0.80.\n"]
    for group in groups:
        sections.append(f"## {group}\n\n{metrics.to_markdown(results, group)}\n")
    (out_dir / f"{args.split}_report.md").write_text("\n".join(sections))
    print("\n".join(sections[:4]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""From per-train delay distributions to the chance that a change, and a journey, works out.

Transfer times are applied here, after the model. A change works when both trains run
and the planned buffer plus the connecting train's departure delay covers the arriving
train's delay plus the minimum transfer time. Trains are treated as independent, which
is optimistic when one disruption hits both; DB holding a connecting train is not modelled.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TrainForecast:
    """A train's delay at one stop: P(delay = k minutes | runs) for k = 0.., and P(cancelled)."""

    probs: np.ndarray
    p_cancel: float = 0.0

    def normalised(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """The delay distribution scaled to sum to one."""
        total = float(np.sum(self.probs))
        if total <= 0:
            raise ValueError("delay distribution has no mass")
        return np.asarray(self.probs, dtype=np.float64) / total


def change_probability(arriving: TrainForecast, departing: TrainForecast, planned_buffer: float,
                       min_transfer: float) -> float:
    """P(both trains run and arrival delay - departure delay <= planned buffer - minimum transfer).

    Args:
        arriving: The incoming train's arrival delay at the change station.
        departing: The connecting train's departure delay at the change station.
        planned_buffer: Minutes between planned arrival and planned departure.
        min_transfer: Minutes needed to change, e.g. from RIS::Stations connecting times.
    """
    a, d = arriving.normalised(), departing.normalised()
    # Distribution of (arrival delay - departure delay): convolve with the reversed departure pmf.
    diff = np.convolve(a, d[::-1])
    offsets = np.arange(diff.size) - (d.size - 1)
    slack = np.floor(planned_buffer - min_transfer)
    p_made = float(diff[offsets <= slack].sum())
    return (1 - arriving.p_cancel) * (1 - departing.p_cancel) * p_made


def journey_probability(changes: list[tuple[TrainForecast, TrainForecast, float, float]],
                        final_arrival: TrainForecast | None = None, arrival_slack: float | None = None) -> dict:
    """Chain the changes of a journey into one success probability.

    Each change is ``(arriving, departing, planned_buffer, min_transfer)``. Changes are
    multiplied as if independent. A connecting train's departure delay and its later
    arrival delay are correlated, so this is an approximation that ignores that link.

    Args:
        changes: The journey's changes in order.
        final_arrival: The last train's arrival delay at the destination, if a deadline matters.
        arrival_slack: Minutes of lateness at the destination the traveller can absorb.

    Returns:
        Per-change probabilities and the probability that the whole plan works.
    """
    per_change = [change_probability(*change) for change in changes]
    success = float(np.prod(per_change)) if per_change else 1.0
    if final_arrival is not None and arrival_slack is not None:
        pmf = final_arrival.normalised()
        on_time = float(pmf[: int(np.floor(arrival_slack)) + 1].sum())
        success *= (1 - final_arrival.p_cancel) * on_time
    return {"change_probabilities": per_change, "plan_success": success, "plan_fail": 1 - success}


def point(minutes: int, size: int = 1000, p_cancel: float = 0.0) -> TrainForecast:
    """A forecast certain of one delay, handy for tests and fixed timetables."""
    probs = np.zeros(size)
    probs[minutes] = 1.0
    return TrainForecast(probs, p_cancel)

"""Replay the traveller output for recorded trips: typical delay, likely range, chance of being on time.

chance of making the change is added. The connecting train's departure delay is approximated by

"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from connection import TrainForecast, change_probability  # noqa: E402

def summary(row: pd.Series, probs: np.ndarray, p_cancel: float) -> dict:
    """The traveller view of one forecast, next to what actually happened."""
    q = metrics.quantiles_from_distribution(probs[None])[0]
    on_time = float(np.cumsum(probs)[metrics.LATE_MINUTES - 1]) * (1 - p_cancel)
    median, low, high = int(q[metrics.MEDIAN]), int(q[metrics.LOW]), int(q[metrics.HIGH])
    return {
        "example_id": int(row["example_id"]),
        "train": prompts.train_label(row),
        "target_stop": prompts.name(row["k_station"]),
        "planned_arrival": str(row["k_arr_pt"]),
        "headline": f"about +{median} min, likely {low} to {high} min, {on_time:.0%} chance of arriving on time",
        "typical_delay_minutes": median,
        "likely_range_minutes": [low, high],
        "p_on_time": round(on_time, 3),
        "p_cancelled": round(float(p_cancel), 3),
        "rationale": prompts.rationale(row),
        "actual": prompts.target_text(row),
    }


def main() -> None:
    """Load a trained checkpoint, forecast the chosen examples, print JSON."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--examples", default="data/trip/examples.parquet")
    parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", required=True, help="checkpoint.pt written by train.py")
    parser.add_argument("--start-checkpoint", default=START_CHECKPOINT)
    parser.add_argument("--example-ids", type=int, nargs="+", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--buffer", type=float, default=8.0, help="planned minutes between the two trains")
    parser.add_argument("--min-transfer", type=float, default=5.0, help="minutes needed to change")
    parser.add_argument("--device", default="cuda")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    frame = pd.read_parquet(args.examples)
    rows = frame.set_index("example_id").loc[args.example_ids].reset_index()
    model = TripTSLM.from_opentslm_checkpoint(args.start_checkpoint, device=args.device)
    if not model.lora_enabled:
        model.enable_lora()
    model.load_from_file(args.checkpoint)
    model.eval()

    out = model.predict_distribution(collate([prompts.sample(row) for _, row in rows.iterrows()]))
    probs = out["probs"].float().cpu().numpy()
    p_cancel = out["p_cancel"].float().cpu().numpy()
    result = {"forecasts": [summary(row, probs[i], float(p_cancel[i])) for i, (_, row) in enumerate(rows.iterrows())]}
    if len(rows) == 2:
        arriving = TrainForecast(probs[0], float(p_cancel[0]))
        departing = TrainForecast(probs[1], float(p_cancel[1]))
        p_change = change_probability(arriving, departing, args.buffer, args.min_transfer)
        result["change"] = {"planned_buffer_minutes": args.buffer, "min_transfer_minutes": args.min_transfer,
                            "p_change_works": round(p_change, 3),
                            "headline": f"{p_change:.0%} chance of making the change"}
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Raster is a 3-line source, renders on the globe in v5+, and is trivially cacheable by the service worker. Bundle: maplibre ≈ 900 kB min / ≈ 240 kB gzip, precached by the SW. **Offline fallback is built in**: if tiles fail the globe still draws as a dark sphere with the glowing route and station dots on top, which reads as an intentional stylised mode. Add a `NetworkFirst`→`CacheFirst` tile cache and pre-warm it by running presenter mode once on venue wifi. |

## 8. Presenter state machine (`src/features/presenter/steps.ts`)

```ts
export const STEPS = [
  { id: "pain",    panel: "slide:pain",   camera: "globe-idle",   data: "none" },
  { id: "share",   panel: "slide:share",  camera: "globe-idle",   data: "sharedText" },       // share sheet mock + text arriving
  { id: "parsed",  panel: "cards",        camera: "fit-route",    data: "journey", draw: "legs" },
  { id: "predict", panel: "prediction",   camera: "fly-break",    data: "prediction", draw: "recolour+chain+countup" },
  { id: "advise",  panel: "recommend",    camera: "fit-both",     data: "recommendation", draw: "alt-dashed" },
  { id: "proof",   panel: "slide:proof",  camera: "hold",         data: "proof.json|png" },
  { id: "close",   panel: "slide:close",  camera: "globe-home",   data: "none" },
] as const
```
- Entering presenter (`?present=1` or `P`): `runFromSeed()` eagerly so every step's data is already in the store; set `document.documentElement.dataset.present = "1"` (type scale), hide the paste UI, show a 4px step progress bar at the bottom and a faint "3/7" counter.
- Keys: `ArrowRight`/`Space`/`PageDown` → next, `ArrowLeft`/`PageUp` → prev, `Home` → 0, `Esc` → exit, `F` → `requestFullscreen`, `M` → toggle motion. `useEffect` on `presenter.step` runs the step's `camera` and `draw` actions; the draw functions are idempotent so going backwards is safe (re-render at final state instantly).
- User mode is the same component tree driven by `stage` instead of `step` (idle → SharePanel; parsed → cards + fit-route; predicted → prediction + fly-break; done → recommendation). The map choreography functions are shared, so presenter costs only `steps.ts`, the four slide components and the key handler.
- "fly-break" camera: find the first leg whose `missProbability.value` ≥ 0.4 and fly to its `to` station; if none, fit route.
